Para. 189: Prior to that final struggle, the revolutionaries should not
expect to have a majority of people on their side.... the task of
revolutionaries will be less to win the shallow support of the majority
than to build a small core of deeply committed people. As for the
majority, it will be enough to make them aware of the existence of the
new ideology and remind them of it frequently."

Which is why UNAPACK and the NPR radio show were so great! (NPR did 2
short segments on the Unabomber & his supporters last week. I'll see if
I can find transcripts.)

Which is also why we must continue to post here and keep discussing the
matter, and also why we must find other forums to discuss the issues
(such as local and/or underground newspapers). Keep writing, keep
getting others involved in discussions, etc. Because...

note 32 "it is even conceivable (remotely) that the revolution might
consist only of a massive change of attitudes toward technology
resulting in a relatively gradual and painless disintegration of the
industrial system." 

Which is what I think we should aim for, because the alternative would
be either a fascistic bloodbath (if humans engineered the collapse) or a
famine/disease scenario (if the collapse happened naturally, as it
inevitably would.)
